correctness.rationale: For the FCC root lattice D3 the subset-sum diameter bound requires squared lengths of all seven nonempty frame subset sums ≤4 at radius 1. The only nonzero candidates are twelve roots of squared length 2 and six axis vectors ±2e_i of squared length 4. Axial inclusion forces linear dependence. Gram restrictions for three roots leave exactly two inner products −1 and one zero, determinant 4 and hence full lattice bases. The unique orthogonal pair and two compatible third roots give 12×2=24 unordered frames. Four permutation tetrahedra have diameter 2 and radius 1, two regular tetrahedra radius √3/2. The deep-hole (1,0,0) yields classical covering radius ≥1, combined with μ≤κ. This proves all-frame completeness including nonbasis competitors.
